paper.title: ML-Bench&Guard: Policy-Grounded Multilingual Safety Benchmark and Guardrail for Large Language Models
paper.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in cross-linguistic contexts, ensuring safety in diverse regulatory and cultural environments has become a critical challenge. However, existing multilingual benchmarks largely rely on general risk taxonomies and machine translation, which confines guardrail models to these predefined categories and hinders their ability to align with region-specific regulations and cultural nuances. To bridge these gaps, we introduce ML-Bench, a policy-g

summary.core_problem: 多语言 LLM 安全评测和 guardrail 常依赖通用风险 taxonomy 与机器翻译，难以覆盖不同司法辖区的法规差异和文化语境。
summary.importance: 贡献是安全 benchmark 与 guardrail：ML-Bench 从地区法规中抽取风险类别和细粒度规则，覆盖 14 种语言；ML-Guard 使用 Diffusion Large Language Model 作为多语言安全判断模型。对预训练研究的直接价值有限，但对 post-train 安全数据构造和跨语言 alignment 评测有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: ML-Bench 不是把英文安全集翻译成多语言，而是从区域性法律和政策文本出发，构造 jurisdiction-specific 的风险类别、规则和多语言安全数据。ML-Guard 在此基础上训练或构建 dLLM-based guardrail，用于多语言安全判断。摘要未给出 dLLM 选择、训练细节和推理流程。
summary.experiments: 摘要说明覆盖 14 种语言，但未给出样本量、模型规模、baseline、准确率、拒答率、跨语言泛化指标或与现有 guardrail 的数值对比。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign、Fudan University 等。Bo Li 是机器学习安全、鲁棒性和可信 AI 方向知名研究者。

summary_en.core_problem: Multilingual LLM safety benchmarks and guardrails often rely on generic risk taxonomies and machine translation, which miss jurisdiction-specific regulations and cultural context.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a safety benchmark and guardrail. ML-Bench derives risk categories and fine-grained rules from regional regulations across 14 languages, and ML-Guard uses a Diffusion Large Language Model for multilingual safety judgment. It is more relevant to post-training safety data and multilingual alignment evaluation than to base-model pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach: ML-Bench is built from regional legal and policy texts rather than translated English safety datasets. Jurisdiction-specific risk categories and rules guide the creation of multilingual safety data. ML-Guard is then developed as a dLLM-based guardrail for multilingual safety classification. The abstract does not specify the dLLM backbone, training recipe, or inference details.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports coverage of 14 languages but does not provide sample counts, model sizes, baselines, accuracy, refusal metrics, cross-lingual generalization results, or numerical comparisons with existing guardrails.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are affiliated with University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Fudan University, and other institutions. Bo Li is a well-known researcher in ML security, robustness, and trustworthy AI.

recommendation.zh: 安全数据构造角度可留意，尤其是 policy-grounded 多语言标签；dLLM guardrail 若无强对照，先当工程选择看。
recommendation.en: Worth noting for safety-data construction, especially policy-grounded multilingual labels; treat the dLLM guardrail as engineering until strong baselines appear.

paper.title: Simple Self-Conditioning Adaptation for Masked Diffusion Models
paper.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) generate discrete sequences by iterative denoising under an absorbing masking process. In standard masked diffusion, if a token remains masked after a reverse update, the model discards its clean-state prediction for that position. Thus, still-masked positions must be repeatedly inferred from the mask token alone. This design choice limits cross-step refinement. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a simple, yet effective, post-training adaptation for MD

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是 masked diffusion language modeling 里的一个具体但关键的训练—采样错位：标准吸收式 masked diffusion 在每一步都会预测当前位置的 clean token 分布，但如果该位置在 reverse update 后仍保持 masked，模型刚刚得到的 clean-state 估计就被直接丢弃。于是下一步它还得从 mask token 重新猜一遍，而不是在上一步估计的基础上继续修正。这会削弱跨步 refinement，尤其在低步数采样时更明显，因为每一步都需要做更大的去噪推进。
summary.importance: 对新型语言建模范式来说，这篇文章的价值不在于提出全新扩散框架，而在于指出一个很实际的改进方向：离散 masked diffusion 的性能瓶颈，部分来自反复“忘掉自己刚刚的预测”。作者给出的是一种轻量 post-training adaptation，而不是从头重训新架构。这一点很重要，因为 diffusion LM 目前最大的现实问题之一就是训练和采样成本都偏高，任何能复用已有 backbone、只做少量额外训练就换来明显质量提升的方法，都比重新设计大模型更接近可落地。对预训练研究者而言，它提示了一个更一般的问题：在非 AR 生成里，模型中间态是否被有效保留和利用，可能和最终建模质量同样重要。
summary.technical_approach: 方法叫 SCMDM，核心是 self-conditioning，但作者把它放在 masked discrete diffusion 的后训练适配场景里，而不是 continuous diffusion 常见的从头训练范式。具体做法是两遍前向、单模型共享参数。第一遍，输入当前 masked 序列，模型输出 clean-state 预测分布。第二遍，把第一遍的预测 detach 后作为 self-conditioning 信号，再送回同一个 denoiser，与当前 noisy/masked 输入一起生成 refined prediction。损失只施加在第二遍输出上。这样设计有几个关键点。第一，它不引入额外的 recurrent latent state 通路，也不需要辅助 reference model，因此改动小。第二，detach 很重要，它把第一遍当作给第二遍提供条件的“固定草稿”，避免训练不稳定或出现通过第一遍梯度路径投机的情况。第三，作者强调 post-training regime 与 from-scratch regime 不同。连续扩散里常见的做法是以一定概率丢弃 self-conditioning 信号，让模型同时学会 conditioned/unconditioned 两种模式；但在已经收敛的 pretrained MDM 上继续微调时，这种 dropout 反而会伤害 adaptation，因为第一遍预测已经有信息量，再强行混入无条件更新，相当于打断 refinement 过程。文中因此主张 full self-conditioning，即微调阶段始终使用第二遍条件化 refinement。方法层面它与已有离散 self-conditioning 工作的区别主要在三点：不依赖额外架构部件；不需要辅助模型；可以从现有 MDM checkpoint 直接做便宜的后训练适配。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖四个离散生成域：自然语言、分子、基因组序列、离散化图像。对 LLM 研究最相关的是自然语言结果。作者在 OpenWebText 上报告 generative perplexity 从 42.89 降到 23.72，降幅约 44.69%。这个幅度相当大，说明标准 MDM 的一部分损失确实来自跨步信息没有被保留。文中还强调这种收益是在 minimal additional compute 下得到的，说明后训练适配成本相对可控。其他域的结果用于证明方法不是语言特例：QM9 上 validity 从 594.2±9.5 提升到 628.2±15.0，uniqueness 从 539.4±12.6 到 546.6±12.1；基因组建模里 distribution fidelity 在不同 denoising step budget 下最高提升 10.73%；CIFAR-10 离散图像生成的 FID 改善 9.12%。更有价值的是训练策略消融：作者比较了 full self-conditioning 与带随机 dropout 的 partial self-conditioning，发现后训练场景下前者更稳定且效果更好。这一结论比单纯的最终分数更重要，因为它说明 self-conditioning 的最佳用法依赖训练阶段：从头训练时需要兼顾鲁棒性，后训练时更像是“教模型学会 refinement”。如果全文里有 step-budget 对比图，建议重点看低步数采样下的收益，因为那最能体现跨步复用的价值。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇值得泛读偏精读。先看引言和方法图，确认作者指出的 failure mode：clean prediction 在下一步没有被保留。然后重点看 two-pass training 机制，尤其是为什么第一遍输出要 detach、为什么 loss 只放在第二遍。接着看关于 post-training regime 的消融，那里是全文最有信息量的部分，因为它回答了“为什么不沿用 continuous diffusion 里常见的 50/50 dropout self-conditioning”。最后看自然语言实验和 step-budget 结果，判断收益主要来自更好的低步数采样，还是全步数范围都改善。预计 30–45 分钟可以读完关键内容。如果你在关注 MDLM、SEDD、LLaDA 一类离散扩散/掩码生成范式，这篇文章最值得记住的不是具体实现细节，而是一个训练原则：当模型已经有可用的中间 clean estimate 时，应显式把它变成下一步的条件，而不是每一步都从 mask 重新开始。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a specific but important mismatch in masked diffusion for discrete sequence generation. In standard absorbing-mask diffusion, the model predicts a clean-token distribution at each reverse step, but if a position remains masked after the update, that clean-state estimate is discarded. At the next step, the model must infer the token again from the mask symbol rather than refining its previous guess. This weakens cross-step refinement, especially in low-step sampling where each denoising step must make larger progress.
summary_en.importance: For alternative language-modeling paradigms, the contribution is not a new diffusion family but a practical correction to an existing weakness: part of the quality gap in masked discrete diffusion may come from repeatedly throwing away useful intermediate predictions. The method is framed as a lightweight post-training adaptation rather than a from-scratch redesign. That matters because diffusion LMs already face training and sampling cost pressure; a technique that reuses an existing pretrained backbone and adds only modest extra training is much easier to adopt than a new large-scale architecture. More broadly, the paper highlights a general issue for non-AR generation: how intermediate model states are preserved and reused can be as important as the nominal objective itself.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method, SCMDM, applies self-conditioning to masked discrete diffusion in a post-training setting. The training procedure uses two forward passes through the same denoiser. In the first pass, the model takes the current masked/noisy sequence and predicts a clean-state distribution. In the second pass, that prediction is detached and fed back as a self-conditioning signal together with the same current input, producing a refined prediction. The loss is applied only to the second-pass output. Several design choices matter. First, there is no recurrent latent-state pathway and no auxiliary reference model, so the architectural change is small. Second, detaching the first-pass prediction is important: it turns the first pass into a fixed draft for refinement rather than a shortcut gradient path. Third, the paper argues that post-training is a distinct regime from training from scratch. In continuous diffusion, self-conditioning is often dropped stochastically so the model learns both conditioned and unconditioned behavior. Here, once a pretrained MDM already produces informative clean estimates, dropping the self-conditioning signal becomes counterproductive because it mixes refinement updates with weaker unconditional ones. The paper therefore advocates full self-conditioning during adaptation. Relative to prior discrete self-conditioning approaches, the claimed differences are: no extra architectural modules, no auxiliary model, and direct adaptation from an existing pretrained MDM checkpoint.
summary_en.experiments: The evaluation spans four discrete-generation domains: natural language, molecules, genomics, and discretized images. The most relevant result for language modeling is on OpenWebText, where generative perplexity improves from 42.89 to 23.72, a 44.69% reduction. That is a large gain and supports the claim that standard MDMs lose useful information across denoising steps. The paper also emphasizes that these gains come with minimal additional compute, which is important for practical adoption. Outside language, QM9 validity improves from 594.2±9.5 to 628.2±15.0 and uniqueness from 539.4±12.6 to 546.6±12.1; genomic distribution fidelity improves by up to 10.73% across denoising-step budgets; and CIFAR-10 FID improves by 9.12%. The most informative ablation is the comparison between full self-conditioning and partial self-conditioning with stochastic dropout. In the post-training regime, full self-conditioning is consistently stronger, suggesting that adaptation should teach the model to refine its own draft rather than alternate between refinement and unconditional prediction. If the full paper includes step-budget plots, those are especially worth checking because low-step gains are where cross-step reuse should matter most.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is worth more than a quick skim. Start with the introduction and the main method figure to lock in the failure mode: clean predictions are made, then forgotten. Next, read the two-pass training section carefully, especially why the first-pass output is detached and why the loss is placed only on the second pass. Then go to the ablations on post-training versus from-scratch self-conditioning; that is the most informative part of the paper because it explains why the usual 50/50 conditioning dropout from continuous diffusion is not the right default here. Finally, inspect the language results and any step-budget analysis to see whether the gains are concentrated in low-step sampling or persist more broadly. Around 30–45 minutes should be enough to extract the main ideas. If you follow MDLM-, SEDD-, or LLaDA-style discrete diffusion and masked-generation work, the key takeaway is a training principle: once the model has a usable intermediate clean estimate, make it an explicit condition for the next step instead of forcing the model to restart from the mask token every time.

recommendation.zh: 做 diffusion LM 的可以读：它抓住了“masked token 每步从零猜”的真问题，但像是局部补丁，先看方法节和主表，别急着改 prior。
recommendation.en: Worth a look if you work on diffusion LMs: it targets a real pathology in masked denoising, but it still reads like a local patch—check the method and main table before updating your priors.

paper.title: Language Diffusion Models are Associative Memories Capable of Retrieving Unseen Data
paper.abstract: When do language diffusion models memorize their training data, and how to quantitatively assess their true generative regime? We address these questions by showing that Uniform-based Discrete Diffusion Models (UDDMs) fundamentally behave as Associative Memories (AMs) $\textit{with emergent creative capabilities}$. The core idea of an AM is to reliably recover stored data points as $\textit{memories}$ by establishing distinct basins of attraction around them. Historically, models like Hopfield n

summary.core_problem: 论文研究离散语言扩散模型什么时候是在记忆训练样本，什么时候进入能稳定恢复未见样本的生成区间。它把 Uniform-based Discrete Diffusion Models 解释为一种 associative memory，并用 token recovery 和 conditional entropy 来量化训练样本与测试样本周围的吸引盆。
summary.importance: 这是 diffusion LM 方向里比较值得精读的一类工作。贡献不在于提出更强的模型，而在于给离散扩散语言模型提供了一个可操作的机制解释和诊断框架。AR LM 的记忆与泛化通常通过抽取攻击、n-gram overlap 或下游指标间接观察；这篇论文把问题改写成反向去噪动力学中的稳定点和吸引盆问题。对预训练研究的启发有三点。第一，数据规模不只是降低验证 loss，也会改变模型的吸引盆结构：训练样本的局部盆会收缩，而未见样本附近的盆会扩展。第二，conditional entropy 可以作为 token 稳定性的探针，比只看生成样本是否重复训练文本更细。第三，它说明离散 diffusion LM 的“泛化”可以表现为对未见但来自同一数据分布的序列进行恢复，而不是简单地从噪声中生成新文本。
summary.technical_approach: 论文聚焦 UDDM，即以 uniform corruption 为前向噪声过程的离散扩散模型。模型在反向过程中学习条件分布，用局部条件似然来预测被破坏 token。作者把这种条件似然最大化与 associative memory 联系起来：传统 Hopfield network 依赖显式 energy function 来定义稳定吸引子，但 feed-forward Transformer 一般没有对称权重结构，也不适合强行写成能量模型。论文的关键转向是放弃显式 energy 要求，改用 pseudo-likelihood / conditional likelihood 的动力学视角。简化分析表明，最大化条件似然会隐式产生类似 Hebbian learning 的效应，同时扩大分类 margin，从而在数据点附近形成吸引盆。这个桥接很重要，因为它把离散扩散 LM 的训练目标和记忆系统的恢复动力学接在了一起。方法上，论文用两类探针观察这个结构：token recovery rate 测量被噪声破坏后是否能恢复原 token；conditional entropy 测量模型在给定上下文和扩散步时对 token 的不确定性。低 entropy 且恢复成功的 token 对应更稳定的局部吸引结构。
summary.experiments: 实验围绕训练集大小驱动的 memorization-to-generalization transition 展开。小训练集阶段，模型能较可靠地恢复训练样本 token，但对测试样本 token 不稳定，经常在反向扩散中改写未见序列。随着训练样本数增加，训练点周围的吸引盆不再无限扩张，反而逐渐收缩；同时，来自同一数据分布的测试序列周围开始出现局部稳定区域。进入泛化区间后，模型不仅能保留未被破坏的测试 token，也能从部分破坏的测试序列中恢复 token。论文用 token-level conditional entropy 解释不同恢复行为：成功恢复的 token 通常接近零熵，失败或不稳定 token 的 entropy 更高。sequence-level conditional entropy 则用于检测整体转变；当进入泛化区间后，训练序列与合成序列的 entropy 分布趋于对齐。给出的正文片段没有包含具体模型参数量、语料规模和精确数值表，因此关键应读作趋势和机制证据，而不是可直接外推到 frontier-scale 模型的 scaling law。
summary.reading_guide: 建议精读。先看 Introduction 中对 associative memory、memory blackout、generalization phase 的定义，避免把“retrieving unseen data”误读成隐私泄漏意义上的训练集记忆。再看理论部分，重点是 conditional likelihood 为什么足以形成吸引盆，以及它如何在简化设定中对应 Hebbian learning 和 margin maximization。实验部分重点看 Fig. 1、Fig. 2 和 Fig. 3：这些图展示训练样本与测试样本 token recovery 随训练集大小变化的差异。Fig. 4 的 sequence-level conditional entropy 更适合当作诊断指标来读。值得深挖的问题有两个：一是这个 AM 视角能否解释 MDLM、SEDD、LLaDA 等不同 mask/noise schedule 下的差异；二是 conditional entropy 能否在大规模 diffusion LM 训练中作为数据重复、过拟合或泛化相变的在线监控信号。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies when discrete language diffusion models memorize training examples and when they enter a regime where unseen samples from the same data distribution become stable under the reverse denoising dynamics. It frames Uniform-based Discrete Diffusion Models as associative memories and measures the basin structure through token recovery and conditional entropy.
summary_en.importance: This is a useful paper for researchers following non-autoregressive language modeling. Its main contribution is not a better model recipe, but a mechanistic and measurable account of memorization and generalization in discrete diffusion LMs. The associative-memory view turns a vague question, whether the model memorizes or generalizes, into a question about attractors, basins, and token stability. For pretraining, the important implication is that increasing data size can change the geometry of retrieval: basins around individual training examples shrink, while partial basins around unseen but in-distribution examples expand. This gives a more precise lens for studying data scale, memorization, and generalization in diffusion-style language models.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper focuses on UDDMs, where the forward process corrupts discrete tokens toward a uniform distribution and the reverse model learns conditional token distributions. The key conceptual move is to connect conditional likelihood maximization to associative memory. Classical Hopfield-style memories use explicit energy functions to guarantee stable attractors, but generic feed-forward networks and Transformers do not naturally satisfy the symmetry constraints required by such energy formulations. The authors instead use a pseudo-likelihood or conditional-likelihood perspective: if a model learns to reconstruct tokens from corrupted contexts, the induced reverse dynamics can form basins of attraction around data points. In a simplified setting, the analysis shows that maximizing conditional likelihood implicitly enforces a Hebbian-like update on data points and increases classification margins. Empirically, token recovery rate probes whether a corrupted sequence returns to a given sample, while conditional entropy measures how stable and confident the local token prediction is.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments examine how the retrieval behavior changes as the training set size grows. In the memorization regime, the model reliably recovers training examples but treats unseen test sequences as unstable, often altering their tokens during reverse denoising. As more data are added, the basins around individual training examples become less dominant, and unseen in-distribution examples begin to acquire partial basins. In the generalized regime, the model tends to preserve uncorrupted test tokens and can recover tokens from partially corrupted test sequences. Token-level conditional entropy separates these behaviors: successfully recovered tokens have near-zero entropy, while unstable or incorrectly recovered tokens have higher entropy. Sequence-level conditional entropy is used as a practical transition detector; once the generalized regime is reached, the entropy distributions of training and synthetic sequences align. The provided text does not include concrete parameter counts, dataset sizes, or full numeric tables, so the safest reading is as a mechanism and diagnostic study rather than a scale-calibrated benchmark.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read it carefully if you work on diffusion LMs, masked language modeling, or memorization diagnostics. Start with the introduction’s definitions of associative memory, memory blackout, and the generalization phase, because these terms determine how the claims should be interpreted. Then focus on the theory section linking conditional likelihood to Hebbian learning and margin maximization. In the experiments, prioritize Fig. 1 to Fig. 3 for token recovery dynamics and Fig. 4 for sequence-level conditional entropy. Two follow-up questions are worth tracking: whether the same basin picture holds for MDLM, SEDD, LLaDA, and other masking schedules, and whether conditional entropy can serve as an online signal for overfitting or phase transitions during large-scale diffusion LM pretraining.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会改你看 diffusion LM 的角度：别只盯 perplexity，要看它是在形成训练样本吸引域还是测试样本吸引域；建议先复现 transition 曲线，再谈范式优劣。
recommendation.en: This changes how to inspect diffusion LMs: stop looking only at perplexity and ask whether they form attraction basins around train or test samples; reproduce the transition curve before making paradigm claims.
